body:
## Summary
This comprehensive refactoring addresses critical violations identified by objective code review, implementing the "real testing over mocks" and "fail fast and loud" principles throughout the test suite.

## Critical Fixes

### High Priority Violations (Fixed)
- **Delete test_cli_tools_integration.py**: Removed file containing critical mock violations using patch(subprocess.run) which violated real testing principles
- **Remove duplicate TestArxivIntegration class**: Cleaned up dead code from test_cli_integration.py  
- **Fix overly defensive email error handling**: Updated email integration tests to use check=True and fail fast on subprocess errors, eliminating defensive patterns that silently swallowed failures

### Medium Priority Violations (Fixed)
- **Remove patch usage from notes tests**: Eliminated all patch("pathlib.Path.home") usage by creating isolated storage managers with temporary directories, avoiding mocking need

### Low Priority Tasks (Completed) 
- **Investigate if __name__ == '__main__' blocks**: Confirmed all instances are legitimate entry points for CLI tools and servers, not dead code

## Technical Improvements

### Test Architecture Changes
- **Real subprocess testing**: CLI integration tests now use actual subprocess calls with temporary files instead of mocked parameter parsing
- **Fail fast error handling**: Email tests use check=True and surface errors immediately  
- **Isolated test storage**: Notes tests use custom storage managers with temporary directories instead of mocking the home directory
- **Systematic mock elimination**: Removed pytest-mock and pyfakefs dependencies

### CI Infrastructure
- **Enhanced email testing**: Added msmtp, offlineimap3, and notmuch system dependencies
- **Test environment variables**: Added GMAIL_TEST_PASSWORD for email integration tests
- **Better test markers**: Added "slow" marker to eliminate pytest warnings

### Philosophy Enforcement
- **Real testing over mocks**: All tests now use real tools and actual I/O operations
- **Fail fast and loud**: Tests surface errors immediately instead of defensive handling
- **100% philosophical consistency**: Test suite now aligns with core development principles

## Test Results
- ✅ 471 tests passing, 2 skipped
- ✅ 70% test coverage maintained
- ✅ All mock violations eliminated  
- ✅ CI infrastructure enhanced for real email testing

- [x] All unit tests pass with real testing patterns
- [x] All integration tests use actual tools and subprocess calls
- [x] Email integration tests configured for CI with proper dependencies
- [x] Notes tests use isolated storage without mocking
- [x] CLI tests use real JSON parameter parsing with temp files

body:
This PR fixes critical compilation errors in the NFT marketplace and royalty distributor contracts, improving their integration and overall functionality.

## Changes Made

### 🔧 Bug Fixes
- **Fixed trait declaration issue**: Resolved "undeclared trait" error in nft-marketplace.clar by properly defining and importing the royalty distributor trait
- **Fixed naming conflict**: Resolved "NameAlreadyUsed" error for `block-height` keyword in royalty-distributor.clar by renaming conflicting variables
- **Fixed trait method signature**: Updated trait definition to match actual function names (`distribute-royalty` instead of `receive-royalty`)

### 🚀 Improvements
- **Enhanced contract integration**: Added proper trait-based communication between marketplace and royalty distributor
- **Backward compatibility**: Maintained existing `purchase-nft` function while adding new `purchase-nft-with-royalty` function
- **Code organization**: Better separation of concerns between basic marketplace functionality and advanced royalty features

### 📋 Technical Details
- Updated `royalty-distributor.clar`:
  - Renamed `block-height` fields to `height` in data maps
  - Added proper trait definition for contract integration
  - Improved variable naming to avoid reserved keyword conflicts

- Updated `nft-marketplace.clar`:
  - Added `use-trait` import for royalty distributor integration
  - Simplified original `purchase-nft` function to avoid trait dependency
  - Added new `purchase-nft-with-royalty` function with proper trait usage

## Testing
- [x] Contracts compile successfully with `clarinet check`
- [x] No more compilation errors
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained

## Breaking Changes
None - all existing functionality is preserved.
```

This PR description provides a comprehensive overview of the changes, making it easy for reviewers to understand what was fixed and why.

body:
## Key Features

**Subscription Management System**
- Users can subscribe to specific energy devices with predefined energy amounts and intervals
- Prepaid balance system eliminates transaction friction and ensures payment security
- Price protection through maximum price-per-watt limits prevents unexpected cost increases
- One subscription per user per device maintains clear ownership and prevents conflicts

**Automated Execution Engine**
- Block-height based scheduling ensures predictable execution timing
- Automated energy transfers when subscriptions become due
- Platform fee collection integrated into subscription payments
- Transaction recording maintains complete audit trail

**Financial Controls**
- Prepaid balance management with top-up functionality
- Automatic refund processing upon subscription cancellation
- Price ceiling protection prevents execution above user-defined limits
- Real-time balance tracking and insufficient funds prevention

**User Experience Enhancements**
- Subscription status monitoring with execution readiness indicators
- Historical execution tracking with comprehensive statistics
- Flexible subscription modification for price thresholds
- Seamless integration with existing user profiles and reputation system

## Technical Implementation

The subscription system leverages Stacks block height for reliable scheduling, implements proper STX escrow through contract-owned funds, and maintains referential integrity between users, devices, and subscriptions. The system includes comprehensive error handling for edge cases and maintains consistency with existing transaction patterns.

This feature significantly reduces manual intervention required for regular energy purchases while providing producers with predictable revenue streams, creating a more efficient and user-friendly energy marketplace.

author: paperboardofficial
body: ### Related GitHub Issue Closes: #4787 ### Roo Code Task Context (Optional) ### Description I tried different ways. One was the most trivial one: use `remark-gfm` but it didn't render the tables properly. So, I wrote a custom table parser file. I took inspiration from one of my previous [work](https://github.com/steel-dev/surf.new/blob/main/components/markdown/TableParser.tsx), though I altered it according to our usecase. First, I tried plugging the code in MarkdownBlock.tsx but I found out that it only rendered tables when they came wrapped in backticks (```). But this was not good because most of the time llms would return table that are not encapsulated in backticks. So, I plugged the code in Markdown.tsx file. But the problem came that sometimes the table data came mix with normal text. For example: ``` Here is your comparison table: Header1 | Header2 | Value1| Value2 ``` Hence I wrote a function called `splitMarkdownAndTables` to split the normal text from table. I have also added 2 test files and 26 unit tests. If you want to test it, you can prompt `Give me difference between proxy and vpn in a table`. The code will properly handle tables if they are wrapped in backticks (```) or not. The code will also handle tables which has urls. The code will also handle bold text or strikethrough text. ### Test Procedure ### Pre-Submission Checklist - [x] **Issue Linked**: This PR is linked to an approved GitHub Issue (see "Related GitHub Issue" above). - [x] **Scope**: My changes are focused on the linked issue (one major feature/fix per PR). - [x] **Self-Review**: I have performed a thorough self-review of my code. - [x] **Testing**: New and/or updated tests have been added to cover my changes (if applicable). - [x] **Documentation Impact**: I have considered if my changes require documentation updates (see "Documentation Updates" section below). - [x] **Contribution Guidelines**: I have read and agree to the [Contributor Guidelines](/CONTRIBUTING.md). ### Screenshots / Videos ### Documentation Updates ### Additional Notes ### Get in Touch ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds custom table rendering in markdown with `splitMarkdownAndTables` and `TableParser`, including extensive tests. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds table rendering in `Markdown.tsx` using `splitMarkdownAndTables` to separate text and tables. > - Introduces `parseTable` in `TableParser.tsx` to parse and render markdown tables. > - Handles inline markdown in tables using `parseInlineMarkdown` in `InlineParser.tsx`. > - **Tests**: > - Adds `MarkdownTableIntegration.spec.tsx` with 13 tests for markdown table integration. > - Adds `TableParser.spec.tsx` with 14 tests for table parsing and inline markdown. > - **Misc**: > - Mocks `MarkdownBlock` and `useExtensionState` in tests for consistent environment. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=RooCodeInc%2FRoo-Code&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for b990949477f5b44126cbee5393b480d9e5f222fd. body:
# 📦 PR #38: Refactor — Cambio de configuraciones para los `process.env`

🔗 **Enlace a la PR:** [#38 en GitHub](https://github.com/muke78/Backend_RESTFULL/pull/38)  
🧑‍💻 **Autor:** [@muke78](https://github.com/muke78)  
🔀 **Rama:** `refactor/connection_db` → `dev`  
📅 **Fecha de merge:** 2025-07-12  
✅ **Estado:** Mergeada  

---

## ⏩ Objetivo principal

Esta PR introduce una reestructuración en la gestión de variables de entorno (`process.env`) en el proyecto, mejorando la configuración y el manejo de entornos para la conexión a la base de datos y otros servicios.  
El objetivo es lograr un código más **limpio**, **seguro** y **fácil de mantener**.

---

## 📝 Cambios principales

- ♻️ **Refactorización** de la carga y uso de variables de entorno:  
  Se centralizó la obtención de datos sensibles y configuraciones usando `process.env`, eliminando duplicidad y asegurando que toda la app utilice valores provenientes del entorno.

- 🐞 **Corrección de bugs** de configuración:  
  Se corrigieron errores relacionados con la obtención y uso de variables de entorno, evitando valores *hardcodeados* y permitiendo una mejor adaptación a distintos ambientes (desarrollo, producción, testing).

- 🚀 **Mejora de rendimiento y seguridad:**  
  Ahora la configuración es más flexible y segura, evitando exponer información crítica en el código fuente y permitiendo la configuración vía archivos `.env`.

- 📄 **Mejor documentación interna:**  
  Se añadieron comentarios y se mejoraron las instrucciones en el código para facilitar la comprensión de la nueva estructura de configuración.

---

## 📂 Archivos afectados

Se modificaron **19 archivos** en total, incluyendo:

- Módulos de conexión a la base de datos  
- Archivos de configuración  
- Servicios que dependían de variables de entorno

---

## ✨ Importancia de los cambios

- 🔧 **Mantenibilidad:**  
  Permite modificar configuraciones sin tocar el código fuente.

- 📈 **Escalabilidad:**  
  Facilita la incorporación de nuevos entornos o la migración a infraestructuras distintas.

- 🔐 **Seguridad:**  
  Disminuye el riesgo de exponer información sensible.

- 📚 **Buenas prácticas:**  
  Cumple con estándares recomendados para aplicaciones Node.js.

---

## 📊 Estadísticas

- 📁 Archivos modificados: **19**  
- ➕ Líneas añadidas: **102**  
- ➖ Líneas eliminadas: **128**

---

## 🏷️ Etiquetas asociadas

`refactor ♻️`, `fix 🔧`, `performance 🚀`, `documentation 📖`, `bug 🐛`

author: maleknoureddine
body:
# Add Comprehensive Testing Infrastructure and Code Quality Improvements

## Overview
This PR introduces a complete testing infrastructure for the Bookify application, including unit tests, integration tests, functional tests, and architecture tests. Additionally, it includes various code quality improvements, bug fixes, and refactoring to enhance maintainability and enforce architectural constraints.

## Changes Made

### 🧪 Testing Infrastructure

#### Domain Layer Testing
- **New Project**: `Bookify.Domain.UnitTests` for testing domain entities and services
- Comprehensive unit tests for `Booking`, `PricingService`, and `User` functionalities
- Created `ApartmentData` and `UserData` classes for consistent test data management
- Established base test class for common testing utilities
- Added global using directives for improved test code readability

#### Application Layer Testing
- **New Project**: `Bookify.Application.UnitTests` for testing application services
- Added `InternalsVisibleTo` attribute for unit test access
- Implemented comprehensive unit tests for `ReserveBookingCommandHandler` covering various scenarios
- Created dedicated test data classes for consistent test setup

#### Integration Testing
- **New Project**: `Bookify.Application.IntegrationTest` for integration testing
- Added `InternalsVisibleTo` attribute for integration test access
- Updated solution configuration for the new integration test project

#### Functional Testing
- **New Project**: `Bookify.Api.FunctionalTests` for end-to-end API testing
- Implemented `BaseFunctionalTest` for common test functionalities
- Created `FunctionalTestWebAppFactory` with PostgreSQL, Redis, and Keycloak setup
- Added comprehensive test classes for user login, registration, and user information retrieval
- Included `bookify-realm-export.json` for Keycloak realm configuration

#### Architecture Testing
- **New Project**: `Bookify.ArchitectureTests` for validating architectural constraints
- Implemented tests for naming conventions and access modifiers
- Added validation for command/query handlers and validators
- Created tests to ensure domain events are sealed and entities have private constructors
- Established layer dependency tests to maintain proper separation of concerns

### 🔧 Code Quality Improvements

#### Bug Fixes and Typos
- Fixed typos in `ReserveBookingCommandHandler.cs` and `Booking.cs`
- Corrected "NotFount" to "NotFound" in relevant files
- Fixed spelling of `ReserveBookingCommandHandler` for consistency

#### Refactoring and Encapsulation
- Refactored access modifiers from `public` to `internal` for several classes
- Changed domain event records from `public record` to `public sealed record` for immutability
- Modified `Apartment` constructor to set `lastBookedOnUtc` to current UTC time
- Renamed `IsOverlaping` to `IsOverlapingAsync` in repository interfaces

#### Error Handling Improvements
- Created `ApartmentErrors` class for centralized apartment-related error handling
- Refactored `ReserveBookingCommandHandler` to utilize new error handling approach

### 🔐 Authentication and Configuration Updates
- Changed unauthorized response in `UsersController` from `BadRequest` to `Unauthorized`
- Reduced minimum password length in `RegisterUserCommandValidator` from 5 to 3
- Updated `AuthenticationOptions` to allow modification of `ValidIssuer` and `MetadataUrl`
- Changed properties in `KeycloakOptions.cs` from `init` to `set` for flexibility

### 📝 Development Experience
- Added optional data seeding remark in `Program.cs` for development environment
- Removed unnecessary global using directive for Xunit in test files
- Updated all solution configurations for Debug and Release builds

## Impact
- **Test Coverage**: Comprehensive testing at all layers (Domain, Application, Integration, Functional, Architecture)
- **Code Quality**: Improved encapsulation, error handling, and architectural constraints
- **Maintainability**: Better separation of concerns and consistent naming conventions
- **Developer Experience**: Enhanced development workflow with proper test infrastructure

## Testing
All new test projects have been added with appropriate configurations and dependencies. The testing infrastructure supports:
- Unit testing for business logic validation
- Integration testing for component interaction
- Functional testing for end-to-end scenarios
- Architecture testing for constraint validation

author: jrpie
body:
After PR #48 there still remains a case where vimv can overwrite files:
Suppose the directory structure is
```
.
├── myfile
└── t
    └── myfile
```
vimv will show
```
myfile
t
```

Renaming myfile to t/myfile will cause an overwrite.
Moreover the directory structure might have changed since the user started vimv.

This PR adds a check to never overwrite files ever. A warning is printed, but the renaming process continues, as it is probably easier to recover from a situation where one file was not moved correctly then from the situation where vimv stopped working in the middle of the renaming process.
Furthermore the PR reduces code duplication.

- hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac (manual salt + custom iterations) Includes verification for bcrypt and shows how to generate salts using the secrets module

author: xtremekforever
body:
Update llhttp dependency in `CNIOLLHTTP` target ahead of adding a new patch to the `update_and_patch_llhttp.sh` script.

### Motivation:

We need to update the `update_and_patch_llhttp.sh` script to add an additional patch to fix compiling swift-nio with C++ interop enabled in Swift targets. It was recommended to update llhttp separately from the patch update and ahead of time to keep the changes separate from each other.

### Modifications:

Ran the `update_and_patch_llhttp.sh` script in the CNIOLLHTTP target to update the llhttp dependency to the latest version (9.3.0). It appears that the only changes from 9.2.1 (previous version) is a few new includes, and the definition of the `UNREACHABLE` macro that is used instead of the `abort()` call.

### Result:

Everything compiles locally and test suite passes with these changes.

@Lukasa

author: bnm12
body:
I've added a new "blip" result to the SIN check, which occurs when the number of hits is equal to the SIN rating.

The SIN check results are now as follows:
- success: hits - sinRating < 0
- blip: hits - sinRating === 0
- flagged: hits - sinRating === 1
- burned: hits - sinRating >= 2

The `sincheckresult` type and the `checkSin` function have been updated to reflect these changes. I've also updated the tests to cover the new logic.

author: detj
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors authentication mechanism to use a reverse proxy for all API HTTP requests originating from the Dashboard. It also eliminates CORS from API backend. For the nextjs rewirte to work, the environment variable `API_BASE_URL` must be present with a valid HTTP origin for the dashboard (npm run build) to succeed.

- The mechanism of reading and writing cookies hasn't changed. API service will continue to try read tokens from cookies first before falling back to reading from `Authorization` header.
- All nextjs routes continue to set cookies to avoid any major disruptions.
- No environment variables for API or Dashboard has changed, again to ensure no major disruptions and easier upgrades.

## Tasks

### Backend

- [x] Remove CORS as it is no longer required
- [x] Remove gin cors module

### Frontend

- [x] Add a nextjs rewrite to proxy all http requests starting with `/api/*`
to proxy to API backend
- [x] Ensure GitHub authentication works with cookies
- [x] Ensure Google authentication works with cookies
- [x] Ensure logout works and clears cookies
- [x] Ensure refresh token mechanism works as expected
- [x] Ensure no auth API call goes to API backend endpoint directly
- [x] Prefixed all frontend api calls with `/api/*`
- [x] Removed a benign console.log line from filters.tsx
- [x] Replaced an incorrect `<text>` tag with `<span>` in layout.tsx.
`<text>` is not an HTML tag.

> [!NOTE]
>
> There's a lot of formatting changes to `.tsx` files. Bear with me and try to ignore them for now.

## See also

- fixes #2401

author: mintesnotebanksira
body:
## Summary
- Adds Google OAuth2 authentication as a FastAPI dependency for all main API endpoints.
- Allows any Google account to access the system (no domain restriction).
- Minimal backend changes: new dependency in requirements, new utils/google_auth.py, and router dependency injection.
- Frontend must send a valid Google ID token in the Authorization header.

## Details
- Uses google-auth to verify Google ID tokens.
- If the token is valid and contains an email, access is granted.
- All /api/batches, /api/problems, and /api/generation endpoints are now protected.
- No user database or session management required.

## Motivation
This enables secure, Google-based authentication for the API with minimal code changes, supporting any Google user.

author: jlowin
body:
This PR builds on the recently merged #1128 fix for empty OpenAPI parameters by expanding the filtering logic and adding comprehensive test coverage.

## Problem
PR #1128 fixed empty parameters in deep object and array handling code paths, but empty collections could still fall through to the general parameter handling logic and be included in HTTP requests.

## Solution
- **Enhanced filtering**: Added comprehensive empty collection filtering at the initial parameter selection stage, ensuring empty arrays and dicts are excluded before any processing
- **Complete coverage**: Now handles all empty parameter scenarios, not just deep objects and arrays  
- **Type safety**: Fixed type checking issues with proper value extraction

## Testing
Added two new test cases:
- `test_empty_array_parameter_exclusion`: Verifies empty arrays (`[]`) are completely excluded from query parameters
- `test_empty_deep_object_parameter_exclusion`: Verifies empty dicts (`{}`) with deepObject style are excluded

All existing tests continue to pass, ensuring no regressions.

## Result
Complete adherence to documented behavior: *"FastMCP only includes query parameters that have non-empty values"*

### **User description** ### 🔗 Related Issues https://github.com/SeleniumHQ/selenium/issues/15801 ### 💥 What does this PR do? This PR ensures that the Selenium Manager test suite passes on Linux arm64, and enables CI tests for this platform through GitHub's [recently released Linux arm64 runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-01-16-linux-arm64-hosted-runners-now-available-for-free-in-public-repositories-public-preview/). ### 🔧 Implementation Notes I'm new to Rust, but wanted Selenium Manager to explicitly fail if users try to run it for Chrome or Edge on Linux arm64, since it's not supported. Previously, the code would silently download `linux64` binaries which are for Linux x64, and cause segfaults on Linux arm64. The setup I went for at least ensures that Firefox/Geckodriver on Linux arm64 will work and are tested properly as well. ### 💡 Additional Considerations The docs at https://www.selenium.dev/documentation/selenium_manager/#alternative-architectures will need to be updated if the team is open to merging this PR. author: pmboutet
body:
## 🐛 Fix Docker Deployment Issues

Ce PR résout les problèmes de déploiement Docker identifiés et améliore significativement l'infrastructure de déploiement.

### 🔍 Problème résolu

L'erreur `npm ci can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync` empêchait le build Docker. Le package-lock.json était obsolète avec de nombreuses versions incompatibles.

### 🛠️ Solutions implémentées

#### 1. **Synchronisation des dépendances**
- ✅ Suppression de l'ancien package-lock.json obsolète
- ✅ Génération automatique d'un nouveau lock file dans le Dockerfile
- ✅ Utilisation de `npm install --package-lock-only` pour la synchronisation

#### 2. **Dockerfile multi-stage optimisé**
- ✅ Stage builder pour les dépendances et compilation
- ✅ Stage production minimal et sécurisé
- ✅ Utilisateur non-root pour la sécurité
- ✅ Healthcheck intégré
- ✅ Labels OCI standards

#### 3. **Scripts d'automatisation**
- ✅ `scripts/build-docker.sh` - Build automatisé avec tests
- ✅ `scripts/healthcheck.sh` - Monitoring du container  
- ✅ `scripts/validate.sh` - Validation complète de l'installation

#### 4. **Docker Compose multi-environnement**
- ✅ Services pour production, développement et tests
- ✅ Gestion des volumes et credentials
- ✅ Profils pour différents cas d'usage

#### 5. **CI/CD GitHub Actions**
- ✅ Pipeline complet avec tests multi-versions Node.js
- ✅ Build multi-architecture (AMD64, ARM64)
- ✅ Scan de sécurité avec Trivy
- ✅ Déploiement automatisé staging/production

#### 6. **Documentation complète**
- ✅ Guide détaillé dans `docs/DOCKER.md`
- ✅ Résumé des corrections dans `DOCKER_FIX_SUMMARY.md`

### 🧪 Tests effectués

```bash
# Build réussi
./scripts/build-docker.sh ✅

# Validation complète
./scripts/validate.sh ✅

# Docker Compose
docker-compose up --build ✅

# Healthcheck
docker run --rm md2googleslides:latest scripts/healthcheck.sh ✅
```

### 📊 Améliorations

- **Sécurité** : Utilisateur non-root, images minimales
- **Performance** : Multi-stage build, optimisation des layers
- **Monitoring** : Healthcheck et scripts de validation
- **Maintenabilité** : Documentation complète et scripts automatisés
- **CI/CD** : Pipeline automatisé pour tous les environnements

### 🏗️ Architecture finale

```
📁 Infrastructure Docker
├── 🐳 Dockerfile (multi-stage optimisé)
├── 🏗️ docker-compose.yml (multi-environnement)
├── 📜 Scripts d'automatisation
├── 📚 Documentation complète
└── ⚙️ CI/CD GitHub Actions
```

### 🚀 Prêt pour la production

Ce PR garantit :
- ✅ Déploiement Docker stable et reproductible
- ✅ Absence de bugs liés aux dépendances
- ✅ Code maintenu à jour pour la production
- ✅ Monitoring et debugging facilités
- ✅ Sécurité renforcée

### 📝 Checklist

- [x] Problème de package-lock.json résolu
- [x] Dockerfile optimisé et sécurisé  
- [x] Scripts d'automatisation fonctionnels
- [x] Docker Compose configuré
- [x] CI/CD pipeline créé
- [x] Documentation mise à jour
- [x] Tests validés

author: kim-se-hee
body:
# 주요 구현 사항
특정 제품의 리뷰를 커서 기반 페이징 방식으로 조회할 수 있는 기능을 구현했습니다.  
정렬 기준은 다음 두 가지 중 하나를 선택할 수 있으며 오름차순과 내림차순이 가능합니다.
- 별점(score) 순
- 등록일(registerDate) 순

## 요청 DTO
커서 기반 페이징을 위해 다음과 같은 정보를 요청합니다.
- lastId: 이전 페이지의 마지막 리뷰 ID
  - 평점과 등록 시각이 동일할 경우 를 위해 리뷰의 id는 반드시 포함합니다. 
- lastScore: 이전 페이지 마지막 리뷰의 별점
- lastRegisterDate: 이전 페이지 마지막 리뷰의 등록일

`@AssertTrue`를 이용해 `lastScore`와 `lastRegisterDate` 중 하나만 입력되었을 때만 유효하도록 검증합니다.  
이는 두 값이 동시에 입력될 경우, 평점과 등록일에 대한 조건이 함께 생성되는 것을 방지하기 위함입니다.

## QueryDSL 기반 동적 리뷰 조회 쿼리

해당 쿼리는 `score` 또는 `registerDate`를 기준으로 커서 기반 페이징을 수행하며, 오름차순 또는 내림차순 정렬을 지원합니다.  
단, `score`나 `registerDate` 값이 동일한 리뷰들 사이에서는 정렬 방향과 관계없이 항상 `id` 기준 오름차순 정렬을 적용합니다.

### sameValuePredicate

`sameValuePredicate`는 커서 기반 페이징을 위한 `BooleanExpression`을 생성하는 과정에서 사용하는 조건입니다.  
이는 `score`나 `registerDate`이 고유 식별자가 아니기 때문에 필요한 조건입니다.

#### 예시

이전 페이지의 마지막 리뷰의 `score`가 5이고, `score` 기준 내림차순 정렬을 요청한 경우 단순히 아래와 같은 조건을 where 절에 적용하면,

```sql
WHERE review.score < 5
```
동일한 5점 리뷰 중 일부만 조회되고, 나머지 5점 리뷰는 건너뛰고 4점 리뷰부터 조회하게 됩니다.

이러한 문제를 방지하기 위해 다음과 같은 조건을 구성합니다:

```sql
(review.score = 5 AND review.id > 39) OR (review.score < 5)
```
즉, 동점자 중 아직 조회되지 않은 항목을 id로 필터링하고, 다음 구간의 리뷰까지 포함하기 위해 OR로 결합하는 방식입니다.

커서 조건 정리을 정리하면 아래와 같습니다.
- 첫 페이지 요청 시: 조건 없음
- 이후 페이지 요청 시:
  - 동점자 조건: review.score = ? AND review.id > ?
  - 비동점자 조건: review.score < ? (또는 > 방향)
  - 두 조건을 OR로 묶어 where 절 구성

# TODO
제품과 리뷰에 대한 핵심 기능 구현을 어느정도 마쳤으며, 복잡한 동적 쿼리를 포함하고 있어 테스트 코드를 작성할 예정입니다.

author: thisislawatts
body: This branch integrates chore notification functionality that was previously hosted within the [Aggregator](https://github.com/MakerSpaceLeiden/aggregator/tree/master/src/aggregator/chores), into this CRM application. The intention of the migration is to avoid making significant changes to the logic. The changes to the CRM include: ### **Core Functionality Added:** - **Event Generation**: Support for both recurrent (cron-based) and single-occurrence chore events - **Notification System**: Email-based reminder system for volunteers with duplicate prevention - **Management Command**: `send_reminders` command for processing scheduled notifications. This can be invoked by a cron job to trigger the reminders. ### **Key Architectural Change:** - **Database-backed Notification Tracking**: Introduced `ChoreNotification` model to replace Redis-based duplicate prevention from the previous implementation. This provides persistent storage and better integration with Django's ORM. ### **Key Components:** - **`chores/core.py`** (417 lines): Core logic for chore events, time calculations, and notification processing - **`chores/models.py`**: Database models for chores, volunteers, and notification tracking - **`chores/management/commands/send_reminders.py`**: Django management command for sending reminders - **`chores/messages.py`**: Email message templates for volunteer reminders ### **Dependencies Added:** - `croniter>=6.0.0` - from aggregator for cron-based scheduling - `humanize>=4.12.3` - from aggregator for human-readable time formatting - `time-machine>=2.16.0` - For time manipulation in tests - `factory-boy>=3.3.3` - For test data generation ### **Minor Changes:** - Added `full_name` property to `User` model in `members/models.py` - Comprehensive test suite with factories and model tests ### **Impact:** This consolidation eliminates the need for a separate service while maintaining the same functionality for chore scheduling and volunteer notification management. The system supports complex scheduling patterns and prevents duplicate notifications through database tracking instead of Redis, providing better persistence and integration with the Django ecosystem. This PR introduces the logic, but it will need to be tied into a cron job on the server before it is functional. Supporting diagrams: Current implementation in Aggregator New implementation

This PR implements a comprehensive modern frontend for the Let's Talk AI chat system, addressing all requirements outlined in the feature request.

## 🚀 Features Implemented

### Dashboard Page
- **Execution History**: Visual display of recent pipeline executions with status indicators
- **System Analytics**: Real-time monitoring of job success rates, execution times, and system health
- **Error Highlighting**: Clear visual indicators for failed jobs and system issues
- **Performance Metrics**: Key performance indicators with trend analysis

### Jobs Management Page
- **Complete Job Listing**: View all configured pipeline jobs with detailed information
- **CRUD Operations**: Full create, edit, and delete functionality for pipeline jobs
- **On-Demand Execution**: Run pipelines manually with real-time status updates
- **Execution History**: Detailed history tracking for each individual job
- **Flexible Scheduling**: Support for cron expressions, intervals, and one-time jobs

### Analytics & Performance Page
- **Performance Trends**: Monthly execution performance with visual charts
- **Success Rate Monitoring**: Track and visualize job success rates over time
- **Resource Usage**: CPU, memory, and disk usage monitoring with progress bars
- **Trend Analysis**: Identify performance patterns and optimization opportunities

### Activity Feed Page

- **Event Tracking**: Monitor job creations, executions, failures, and user actions
- **Historical Data**: Access to comprehensive historical activity data

- **Framework**: Built with Svelte 5 + SvelteKit for modern reactive UI
- **Styling**: TailwindCSS 4 with custom dark theme matching the design requirements

Hello and thank you for your work on this project :)

I want to use pyinfra to enable a nftables service on the boot runlevel with OpenRC. I noticed that the openrc.service operation would always trigger a change on every run even though the service was never really enabled on this runlevel. This is because the change was always happening on the default runlevel, ignoring the configuration.

I would like to propose these changes:
- A noop message for when a service is already enabled/disabled to help with troubleshooting.
- Support for enabled/disabling services on a specific runlevel, as expected from the documentation.

I did not find it necessary to update the openrc.service documentation.
I also fixed a small typo in a link in the contributing documentation.

## Summary

Implements a dynamic countdown banner for the Meowtica Smart Hub product detail pages to promote a limited-time 50% off offer. The banner displays a 15-minute countdown timer and transforms into a promotion announcement when the timer expires.

## Changes Made

### 🎯 Features Implemented
- **Dynamic Countdown Timer**: Real-time 15-minute countdown that updates every second
- **Bilingual Support**: Full Chinese and English language support with proper translations
- **Product-Specific Display**: Banner only appears on Meowtica Smart Hub product pages
- **Promotion End State**: Shows celebratory "🎉 50% OFF NOW ACTIVE!" message when countdown expires
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly layout that adapts to different screen sizes

### 🎨 Design & Styling
- **Visual Consistency**: Uses existing brand colors (accent #00C2A8, secondary-dark #1E1E1E)
- **Eye-catching Design**: Gradient background with accent color highlights and shadow effects
- **Strategic Positioning**: Placed below navigation tabs and above main content as specified
- **Professional Typography**: Clear, readable fonts with proper contrast

- ✅ **Created `src/components/CountdownBanner.tsx`** - Main countdown component
- ✅ **Modified `src/pages/products/[slug].tsx`** - Integrated banner into product page

### 🧪 Testing Verified
- ✅ Banner appears only on Meowtica Smart Hub pages (`/products/meowtica-smart-hub`)
- ✅ Banner does NOT appear on other product pages (confirmed with Purr Motion Sensor)
- ✅ Countdown timer functions correctly in both languages
- ✅ Expired state displays properly with promotion message
- ✅ Responsive design works on different screen sizes
- ✅ No ESLint errors or build issues

```typescript

- useState for countdown state and expiration tracking  
- useEffect with setInterval for real-time updates
- Proper interval cleanup on component unmount
- Conditional rendering based on product slug

| English | "HURRY! Sale ends in" | "🎉 50% OFF NOW ACTIVE!" |

## Motivation
During the investigation, we discovered that KECS uses the k3d Go SDK directly and doesn't actually need the Docker CLI. This presents an opportunity to significantly reduce the image size.

## Changes
1. **Remove Docker CLI from main Dockerfile**
   - Removed Docker CLI installation steps
   - Kept Docker socket mounting capability (required for k3d Go SDK)
   - Image size reduced from ~512MB to ~303MB (40% reduction)

2. **Update docker-entrypoint.sh**
   - Replace `docker version` check with filesystem-level socket readability check
   - Maintains the same functionality without Docker CLI dependency

3. **Migrate Dockerfile.api to Debian base**
   - Changed from Alpine Linux to `golang:1.24.3` base image
   - Resolved glibc compatibility issues
   - Standardized with the main Dockerfile structure

## Image Size Comparison
- **Before**: ~512MB (main Dockerfile with Docker CLI)
- **After**: ~303MB (main Dockerfile without Docker CLI)
- **Dockerfile.api**: ~310MB (includes curl for health checks)
- **Dockerfile.test**: ~154MB (uses distroless, unchanged)

## Testing
- [x] Build tested locally for both amd64 and arm64
- [x] Verified k3d functionality still works without Docker CLI
- [x] Confirmed docker-entrypoint.sh correctly detects socket access

## Test plan
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline passes
- [ ] Docker images build successfully for all architectures
- [ ] KECS can still manage k3d clusters via Docker socket
- [ ] API-only version works with existing Kubernetes clusters

author: muhammadbarznji
body:
This PR enhances the command suggestion system in **bitchat** by implementing a more intelligent command matching algorithm. The new CommandMatcher provides accurate, context-aware command suggestions when users type partial or misspelled commands.

### Issue
**Problem**: Currently, when users type invalid commands, they receive a generic error message without any helpful suggestions:
User types: /joi
System: "unknown command: /joi"

### Solution
Implemented a new `CommandMatcher` system that:

Core Features:
- Smart Command Suggestions
Suggests the closest matching command when the user makes a typo
Example: /joi → "Did you mean: /join?"

- Three-Tier Matching Algorithm
Prefix Matching: /bl → /block
Substring Matching: lock → /block or /unblock
Typo Correction: /jion → /join (using Levenshtein distance)

- Performance Optimized
O(1) exact match lookups
Early termination for expensive operations
Configurable suggestion threshold

### Feature Enablement
This foundational component enables future features:
1. Command auto-complete UI
2. Command search/discovery
3. Contextual command suggestions
4. Command usage analytics

body:
## Overview

This PR addresses multiple critical flaws identified in the PlantGuard AI repository through comprehensive analysis. The changes transform the repository from a basic prototype into a production-ready application with proper security, testing, documentation, and development practices.

## Critical Issues Fixed

### 🔒 Security & Vulnerability Fixes
- **Fixed npm security vulnerabilities**: Resolved 1 low and 4 moderate severity vulnerabilities through `npm audit fix`
- **Added image validation**: Implemented strict file type checking (JPG, PNG, WebP only) and 10MB size limits
- **Enhanced error handling**: Added comprehensive error boundaries and input validation
- **Environment variable setup**: Created `.env.example` template for secure configuration management

### 🔧 Code Quality & Build Issues  
- **Resolved ESLint errors**: Fixed 3 TypeScript build-breaking errors including empty interfaces and require() imports
- **Updated dependencies**: Refreshed outdated browser data (caniuse-lite was 9 months old)
- **Organized code structure**: Added constants file and utility functions for better maintainability
- **Clean builds**: All builds now pass without errors (only 9 warnings remain for shadcn/ui components)

### 🧪 Testing Infrastructure
- **Added comprehensive testing setup**: Integrated Vitest + React Testing Library
- **Created test suite**: 11 passing tests covering image validation and error boundary functionality
- **Test configuration**: Proper TypeScript config, test scripts, and setup files
- **Coverage ready**: Framework ready for test coverage reporting

### 📚 Documentation & Developer Experience
- **Complete README overhaul**: Replaced generic Lovable template with comprehensive setup guide
- **Contributing guidelines**: Added detailed contribution workflow and coding standards
- **Environment setup**: Clear instructions for Supabase and Gemini AI configuration
- **API documentation**: Documented all features, tech stack, and deployment options

## Key Improvements

### Before
```bash
npm run lint    # ❌ 3 errors, 9 warnings
npm run build   # ⚠️ Builds with vulnerabilities 
npm test        # ❌ No testing framework
# No documentation for setup
# Basic error handling
# No image validation
```

### After  
```bash
npm run lint    # ✅ 0 errors, 9 warnings
npm run build   # ✅ Clean build
npm test        # ✅ 11/11 tests passing
# Comprehensive setup docs
# Error boundaries + validation
# Strict image validation
```

### Enhanced Image Upload Component
```typescript
// Before: Basic file reading with no validation
const handleFileChange = (event) => {
  const file = event.target.files?.[0];
  if (file) {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = (e) => onImageUpload(e.target?.result);
    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
  }

Potential fix for [https://github.com/mlco2/codecarbon/security/code-scanning/6](https://github.com/mlco2/codecarbon/security/code-scanning/6)

To address the issue, we need to add an explicit `permissions` block to the workflow. This block should specify the minimal permissions required for the workflow's jobs to function correctly. 

- **General approach:** Add a top-level `permissions` key for the entire workflow to cover all jobs. If specific jobs require additional permissions, we can override the top-level permissions within those jobs.
- **Specific changes:** Update the `.github/workflows/package.yml` file. Add `permissions` at the workflow root level (before `jobs`) and configure it with minimal privileges (e.g., `contents: read`).
- **Implementation details:** The `contents: read` permission will allow read-only access to repository contents, which is sufficient for most operations in the workflow. If specific jobs need write access to specific components (e.g., `pull-requests: write`), this can be added explicitly within those jobs.

This PR adds support for configuring the set of commit characters used in unicode completion within the Coq LSP server and VSCode extension.

### Motivation

Previously, the set of characters that would accept/commit a unicode completion was hardcoded.
The hardcoding of `" "` as a commit char was especially problematic for me, as typing conjunction (`/\`) followed by a spaced would always end up changing it to some unicode completion.

### Changes

- Added a new server configuration option to specify the commit characters for unicode completion.
- Updated the LSP and VSCode extension to respect this configuration.

### Impact

- Customizable unicode completion.
- (Hopefully) No breaking changes; default behavior remains unchanged unless the option is set.

This pull request introduces changes to streamline the preprocessing pipeline, update classification metrics, and adjust image dimensions used in the machine learning workflow. The most significant changes include modifications to how datasets are saved and loaded, updates to classification reports, and the adjustment of image dimensions.

### Dataset Handling Updates:
* [`principal.py`](diffhunk://#diff-b93c5c3a29f1305f8e5bd476f6158c454682cdfa2a2bd9288c731333c67e3cafR36-L43): Changed the dataset saving logic to save the complete dataset (`X_total` and `y_total`) instead of separate training and testing splits. This simplifies the subsequent re-shuffling process in `classificacao_knn.py`.
* [`src/classificacao_knn.py`](diffhunk://#diff-7f518205a06fad43fba5620540820305bcf118c574236b94be6257d69dccafa6L23-R24): Updated the dataset loading logic to use the newly saved `X_total` and `y_total` arrays, removing the need for concatenation of training and testing splits.

### Classification Metrics Updates:
* [`relatorios_classificacao/relat_32x32_SEM_DataAug_Bordas_NAO_REMOVIDAS.txt`](diffhunk://#diff-ea2f8d7a2769a41d5543df5f79d4ecd61304418b005b5586613ea43c32653c9cL2-R33): Updated classification metrics for the 32x32 image dimension, reflecting slight changes in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
* [`relatorios_classificacao/relat_64x64_SEM_DataAug_Bordas_NAO_REMOVIDAS.txt`](diffhunk://#diff-dc541a25da5350c6c54c897f11b9176a68595a9fca5849230ba4322b95d22528L2-R35): Updated classification metrics for the 64x64 image dimension, with improvements in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

### Image Dimension Adjustment:
* [`src/variaveis.py`](diffhunk://#diff-30c64b12e0c5c2eb1bca67aa6b44835129f7c7d172ebe3fa635b097327638305L1-R1): Adjusted the image dimension from 64x64 to 32x32, aligning the preprocessing pipeline with new requirements.

author: drewoldag
body:
Currently the create_trainer and create_validator functions expect that the `train_step` method in the model class will return a "loss" value. 

The user should be free to return and track any metrics produced in the `train_step` method. This change enables that. 

As long as the returned value from `train_step` is a dictionary, the metrics will be recorded in TensorBoard and MLFlow. 

For reference the return dict should look something like this: 

```
return {
    'metric_0': metric_0_value,
    ...,
    'metric_n': metric_n_value,
}
```

- Added comprehensive Windows-specific unit tests

## Changes
- **WindowsKeyStorage**: Full implementation using Windows Credential Management API
  - Stores credentials as CRED_TYPE_GENERIC with CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE
  - Separate credentials for encrypted keys, metadata, and default key
  - JSON serialization with base64 encoding for binary data
- **Error Handling**: Proper handling of Windows-specific errors (access denied, not found, etc.)
- **Credential Management**: Enumeration, persistence, and cleanup functionality
- **Unit Tests**: Windows-specific tests including persistence across instances
- **Documentation**: Detailed Windows implementation guide and troubleshooting

## Implementation Details
- Keys stored in three credential types:
  1. `Tungsten_Nostr_<key_id>`: Encrypted key data
  2. `Tungsten_Nostr_Meta_<key_id>`: Key metadata
  3. `Tungsten_Nostr_Default`: Default key identifier
- Maximum credential size: 512KB (validated in implementation)
- Credentials persist at machine level for current user

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit tests pass on Windows
- [ ] Keys persist across browser restarts
- [ ] Credential Manager shows Tungsten credentials
- [ ] Key enumeration works correctly
- [ ] Default key management functions properly
- [ ] Large metadata handling works
- [ ] Error scenarios handled gracefully

# Release v0.2.3: Complete Macro API, Enhanced Documentation, and Developer Tooling

## Summary

This major release completes the macro ecosystem with fallible variants, delivers comprehensive documentation improvements with clear output examples throughout, introduces cross-platform developer tooling, and significantly enhances the overall developer experience. This represents a substantial evolution of the library with improved API completeness, documentation clarity, and development workflow.

## New Features

### Complete Macro API Coverage
- **New try_app_path! macro** providing fallible path creation returning Result<AppPath, AppPathError>
- **Complete macro syntax coverage** - Both app_path! and try_app_path! support all four syntax variants
- **API symmetry achievement** - Perfect parity between panicking and fallible variants across the entire API
- **Function-based override support** - Added missing fn variants to both macro types for dynamic path resolution

### Cross-Platform Developer Tooling
- **New ci-local.sh script** for comprehensive local CI testing
- **Auto-detection of cargo** across Windows, macOS, and Linux environments
- **Complete CI pipeline locally** - format, clippy, compile, test, and documentation checks
- **Clear error reporting** with timing information and helpful troubleshooting

### Enhanced Documentation System
- **Complete documentation overhaul** with clear output examples showing exact generated paths
- **Enhanced Quick Start sections** with → comments demonstrating actual results for every example
- **Comprehensive macro documentation** covering all four syntax variants with practical examples
- **Updated API design coverage** including all fallible variants and complete function tables
- **Real-world usage patterns** with XDG support examples and deployment scenarios

## Developer Experience Improvements

### Documentation Quality
- **Added clear output indicators** throughout README.md showing exactly what each macro produces
- **Updated all macro examples** with expected results and behavior explanations
- **Enhanced API symmetry documentation** clearly explaining panicking vs fallible patterns
- **Corrected documentation accuracy** regarding override parameter availability and syntax
- **Complete coverage** of all 142 tests with comprehensive examples

### Workflow Enhancements
- **Updated CONTRIBUTING.md** with modern development practices
- **Integration with CI tooling** for consistent local and remote testing
- **Clear setup instructions** for all supported platforms
- **Improved code quality guidelines** and testing requirements

## Quality and Reliability

### Test Infrastructure
- **Enhanced test reliability** with corrected XDG environment variable handling
- **Fixed false positives** in cross-platform environment testing
- **Comprehensive test coverage** - 142 total tests (88 unit + 54 documentation tests)
- **Cross-platform consistency** - all tests pass reliably across Windows, macOS, and Linux

### Code Quality
- **Zero clippy warnings** with strict linting enforcement
- **100% documentation test coverage** - all examples compile and execute correctly
- **Modern Rust syntax** throughout all examples and documentation
- **Consistent API patterns** across all macro variants and method signatures

## API Completeness Achievement

### Complete Function Symmetry
Now featuring perfect API symmetry across all functions:

| **Panicking** | **Fallible** | **Purpose** |
|---------------|--------------|-------------|
| AppPath::new() | AppPath::try_new() | Constructor |
| AppPath::with_override() | AppPath::try_with_override() | With override |
| AppPath::with_override_fn() | AppPath::try_with_override_fn() | With function |
| app_path!() | try_app_path!() | Convenient macros |
| exe_dir() | try_exe_dir() | Directory access |

### Macro Syntax Coverage
Both macro types support identical syntax variants:
- Direct value usage for simple paths
- Environment variable override for deployment flexibility  
- Optional override expressions for complex logic
- Function-based override for dynamic path resolution

## Migration and Compatibility

### No Breaking Changes
All existing app_path! macro usage continues to work unchanged. Libraries can now opt into fallible behavior using try_app_path! for graceful error handling.

### Enhanced Error Handling
try_app_path! returns Result<AppPath, AppPathError> providing specific error types for better error handling and debugging.

## Development Impact

This release transforms the library from a functional path utility into a comprehensive, production-ready solution with:

- **Complete macro ecosystem** supporting both application and library use cases
- **Professional documentation** with clear examples and expected outputs
- **Robust developer tooling** for consistent development across platforms
- **Comprehensive testing** ensuring reliability and cross-platform compatibility
- **Modern development workflow** with local CI capabilities

The library now provides everything needed for both quick prototyping and production deployment with excellent documentation and developer experience.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/DK26/app

author: rubenverg
body:
Many APL glyphs are overstrikes, this PR adds some unbound glyphs that represent common parts that are then used to encode the composite glyphs.

Almost every glyph seemed to use its own style of cancellation (i.e. for going from `=` to `≠`, or from `≡` to `≢`, or from `≈` to `≉`), so I decided to unify them into just three.

It is very likely that other slight changes happened if the original glyphs did not perfectly line up with their components, but none should be noticeable enough to be a problem.

author: jmgress
body:
This commit fixes CWE-23 (Relative Path Traversal) vulnerabilities in `backend/main.py`.

The `clear_log_file`, `rotate_log_file`, and `download_log_file` functions were vulnerable to path traversal attacks. An attacker could provide a malicious `file_path` to access arbitrary files on the system.

This commit sanitizes the `file_path` argument in these functions by using `os.path.normpath` and `os.path.basename` to prevent path traversal attacks. This ensures that the code only operates on files within the intended log directory.

copilot
body:
## 🤖 Quality Analysis Agent Implementation

This PR implements a comprehensive **Quality Analysis Agent** that answers the question "que agente puedo crear?" by providing an intelligent quality monitoring and analysis system for the segver quality management platform.

## ✨ Features Added

### 🔍 Automated Quality Analysis
- **Intelligent Metrics Analysis**: Automatically evaluates quality metrics against defined targets
- **Smart Alert Generation**: Creates prioritized alerts when metrics fall below thresholds
- **Actionable Recommendations**: Provides specific improvement suggestions based on analysis results
- **Confidence Scoring**: Calculates confidence levels for analysis results

### 📊 Comprehensive Dashboard
- **Real-time Overview**: Live dashboard showing key quality statistics
- **Metrics Management**: Detailed view of all quality metrics with status indicators
- **Alert Monitoring**: Centralized alert management with priority levels
- **Historical Analysis**: Track analysis results over time

### 🎯 Quality Metrics Support
The agent supports 5 key quality metric types:
- **Defect Rate** (`defect_rate`)
- **Compliance** (`compliance`) 
- **Efficiency** (`efficiency`)
- **Customer Satisfaction** (`customer_satisfaction`)
- **Process Time** (`process_time`)

### 🚨 Intelligent Alert System
- **Priority Levels**: Urgent, High, Medium, Low
- **Alert Types**: Threshold exceeded, negative trends, anomalies, compliance issues
- **Automatic Generation**: Alerts created when metrics deviate from targets
- **Status Tracking**: Active/resolved alert management

## 🛠️ Technical Implementation

### Backend Components
- **Django Models**: `QualityMetric`, `QualityAnalysis`, `AgentAlert`
- **REST API**: `/agente-calidad/api/analyze/` for automated analysis
- **Admin Interface**: Full Django admin integration for data management
- **Database**: SQLite support for development, MySQL ready for production

### Frontend Components  
- **Modern UI**: Bootstrap 5 responsive design
- **Interactive Dashboard**: Real-time metrics and analysis display
- **Navigation**: Seamless navigation between Dashboard, Metrics, and Alerts
- **Sample Data**: Built-in sample data generation for testing

### Code Structure
```
quality_agent/
├── models.py          # Data models for metrics, analysis, alerts
├── views.py           # Dashboard views and API endpoints  
├── urls.py            # URL routing for agent functionality
├── admin.py           # Django admin configuration
├── templates/         # HTML templates for UI
│   └── quality_agent/
│       ├── dashboard.html     # Main dashboard
│       ├── metrics_list.html  # Metrics overview
│       └── alerts_list.html   # Alerts management
└── management/
    └── commands/
        └── create_admin.py    # Admin user creation
```

## 🖼️ Screenshot

The Quality Analysis Agent provides a professional interface for monitoring quality metrics and managing alerts:

![Quality Agent Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97cd3674-0060-4b07-8eff-7dbf2f1675c5)

## 🚀 How to Use

1. **Access the Agent**: Navigate to `/agente-calidad/` 
2. **Add Sample Data**: Click "Agregar Datos de Prueba" to populate with test metrics
3. **Run Analysis**: Click "Ejecutar Análisis" to perform automated quality analysis
4. **Review Results**: Check the dashboard for metrics status, active alerts, and analysis results
5. **Manage Data**: Use the admin interface at `/admin/` for detailed data management

## 🔧 Configuration

The agent is automatically configured when added to `INSTALLED_APPS`:
```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ... existing apps
    'quality_agent',
]
```

## 📈 Analysis Algorithm

The agent uses a sophisticated analysis algorithm that:
1. Compares current metric values against defined targets
2. Calculates deviation percentages for metrics below target
3. Determines overall status (Good/Warning/Critical) based on percentage of failing metrics
4. Generates specific recommendations for improvement
5. Creates prioritized alerts for metrics requiring attention
6. Assigns confidence scores based on data quality and analysis certainty

## 🎯 Business Value

This Quality Analysis Agent provides immediate value by:
- **Automating Quality Monitoring**: Reduces manual oversight requirements
- **Early Issue Detection**: Identifies quality problems before they escalate  
- **Actionable Insights**: Provides specific recommendations for improvement
- **Centralized Visibility**: Single dashboard for all quality metrics
- **Proactive Alerting**: Notifies stakeholders when intervention is needed

The agent seamlessly integrates with the existing segver quality management system while adding powerful automated analysis capabilities.

body:
This Python module is responsible for dynamically loading a YOLO object detection model based on the selected type of environment: "kara" (land) or "hava" (airborne). It uses the ultralytics YOLO implementation to initialize the model and retrieve the corresponding class names.
Function:
load_model_by_type(model_type)
Loads the appropriate model file depending on the specified model_type:
"kara": Loads a land-based object detection model.
"hava": Loads an airborne object detection model.
Once the model is loaded, it sets the global model and names variables for use in other parts of the application. If an invalid type is provided, it raises a ValueError.
This module helps centralize and automate model selection logic, making it easier to maintain and switch between models in a unified way

author: nielsvanvelzen
body:
To integrate the new fancy playback code with old UI I moved the old MediaManager to an interface and implemented it on a best-effort basis. We still don't use the queue system in its intended way and have a dirty supplier implementation that is just a list of baseitems. However, the queue system is only made for those suppliers to grow in size while fetching and never shrink or grow after they stopped supplying. This did happen with the queue removal function causing very weird states in the app.

Those issues are now fixed, just took me a few hours 🫠.

**Changes**

- Add new AudioQueueBaseRowAdapter
  - Replacement for the ItemAdapter that was maintained by MediaManager
  - Works stand-alone (e.g. it manages its own items)
- Use queue entries instead of just base items in AudioQueueBaseRowItem
- Support _any_ adapter type in ItemLauncher
- Do not reset adapter when items change in AudioNowPlayingFragment
  - This results in cards animating on removal/addition/move/update instead of the row flashing
- Require queue entry for removeFromAudioQueue and playFrom functions in MediaManager
- Allow reading all queue suppliers in a queue
- Allow reading all (non-removed) fetched entries in a queue
  - This is used to update the AudioQueueBaseRowAdapter when entries are removed
- Add indexOf function to a queue
  - This is used to skip ahead in a queue (MediaManager.playFrom)
- Add support for removing entries from a queue
  - This will update internal caches and modify indices accordingly
  - Will automatically skip to next item if the removed item is currently playing
  - This is the primary change of this PR which required a few additional changes
- Update QueueService to always use "entry" instead of the old "item" term
- Update KeyProcessor for all other mentioned changes
- Change RewriteMediaManager.BaseItemQueueSupplier to be immutable
  - Queue additions just add new suppliers
  - Queue removals use the new removal functionality

**Issues**

Fixes #4516
Part of #1057

author: livankov
body:
The edited documentation section demonstrates various functionalities of the Criteria class, when fetching entities.
 
Initially "productRepository" is instantiated via a call to the "create" function of the "RepositoryFactory" class, which returns an object of the type Repository<EntityName>.

Then, the "create" function of the said repository object is called with 'product' as an argument. This function call is totally redundant as it creates an entity with the id passed as a parameter and returns it. 

The returned Entity object is not used anywhere else and doesn't serve any purpose. Furthermore, 'product' is used as an id of the newly created object, which is generally not a good practice, as it doesn't fit the format.  

Thus, the function call to "this.productRepository.create('product')" serves no purpose, other than to confuse new developers and produce unnecessary overhead.

body:
This PR adds minimum token permissions for all GitHub workflow files to improve security posture according to OpenSSF Scorecard recommendations.

## Changes Made

### Root-level permissions added to 8 workflow files:
- **changelog.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **ci.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **codeql_analysis.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **codespell.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **protect-released-changelog.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **links.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **request_codeowners_review.yml**: Added `permissions: { contents: read }`
- **close-stale.yml**: Changed from overly permissive `issues: write, pull-requests: write` to `contents: read`

### Job-level permissions added/updated:
- **links.yml**: Added `issues: write` to `check-links` job (required for creating issues via `peter-evans/create-issue-from-file`)
- **close-stale.yml**: Moved `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` to `stale` job (required for `actions/stale` to close issues/PRs)

## Security Impact

This implementation follows the principle of least privilege by:
1. Setting restrictive root-level permissions (`contents: read`) for all workflows
2. Adding specific write permissions only at the job level where actually needed
3. Including explanatory comments for all write permissions

## Verification

All 13 workflow files now pass the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check:
- ✅ 13 files passed
- ⚠️ 0 files with warnings  
- ❌ 0 files with errors

The changes maintain existing functionality while significantly improving the security posture of the repository.

Fixes #17.

This pull request introduces two major changes: the addition of a new feature for highlighting invalid numbers in the settings repository and a significant reorganization of the `usecases` package in the domain layer. The most important changes are summarized below:

### New Feature: Highlight Invalid Numbers
* Added a new `highlightInvalidNumbers` flow to `AndroidSettingsRepository` to manage the state of highlighting invalid numbers. (`AndroidSettingsRepository.kt`, [data/settings/src/main/java/com/example/data/settings/AndroidSettingsRepository.ktR56-R59](diffhunk://#diff-c9523922259fc2d4e847df28b37bf1582833548cc0ae8bba5a48d879da67685bR56-R59))
* Implemented a `setHighlightInvalidNumbers` method in `AndroidSettingsRepository` to update the preference for highlighting invalid numbers. (`AndroidSettingsRepository.kt`, [data/settings/src/main/java/com/example/data/settings/AndroidSettingsRepository.ktR99-R105](diffhunk://#diff-c9523922259fc2d4e847df28b37bf1582833548cc0ae8bba5a48d879da67685bR99-R105))
* Introduced a new preference key `HighlightInvalidNumbers` in `SettingsPreferenceKeys` with a default value of `true`. (`SettingsPreferenceKeys.kt`, [data/settings/src/main/java/com/example/data/settings/SettingsPreferenceKeys.ktR46-R50](diffhunk://#diff-ce8d272fd3a3413aa4c6d4c19a591004cfa9cca3305033c189b6d3018c9cf430R46-R50))

### Code Reorganization: Domain Layer `usecases` Package
* Refactored the `usecases` package by categorizing use cases into sub-packages such as `game`, `hint`, `input`, `time`, and `visuals`. This improves the structure and maintainability of the codebase. (`ElapsedTimerManager.kt`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-145ed29bfd757163f160a1e5d8319d10e28ca1236f387db383d81434ec55a158L3-R4); `GameManagementUseCases.kt`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1cafa6d2457ec0b1c38af71d641338ef5f55b713cf0cb8a16bda6baa15bb387eL3-R15); `Module.kt`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f97d44336ce3b1437b67b2083ec01f7f3e7de6bc261111998399739097995ac6L3-R24)
* Renamed and moved individual use case files to their respective sub-packages, updating their package declarations accordingly. For example:
  - `GetGameUseCase` moved to `usecases.game`. (`GetGameUseCase.kt`, [domain/game/src/main/java/com/example/domain/game/usecases/game/GetGameUseCase.ktR1-R9](diffhunk://#diff-8132a268f140f4d890cc6dafd2e6fbd39e63abc87c6aab0ed56ca5c00f43f3d2R1-R9))
  - `FocusOnHintCellsUseCase` moved to `usecases.hint`. (`FocusOnHintCellsUseCase.kt`, [domain/game/src/main/java/com/example/domain/game/usecases/hint/FocusOnHintCellsUseCase.ktL1-R1](diffhunk://#diff-7fa524bb3c768a950037648d7930908c4e96725cef7c9591e8abbed0f4a1b9f8L1-R1))
  - `InputNumberUseCase` moved to `usecases.input` and updated to use the new `MarkRuleBreakingCellsUseCase`. (`InputNumberUseCase.kt`, [domain/game/src/main/java/com/example/domain/game/usecases/input/InputNumberUseCase.ktL1-R13](diffhunk://#diff-91e919881ffecfa5f600c53801d6a06c4a09b8c825d7258dac6a8c7a373317a0L1-R13))
* Updated import statements across the domain layer to reflect the new package structure. (`ElapsedTimerManager.kt`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-145ed29bfd757163f160a1e5d8319d10e28ca1236f387db383d81434ec55a158L3-R4); `GameManagementUseCases.kt`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1cafa6d2457ec0b1c38af71d641338ef5f55b713cf0cb8a16bda6baa15bb387eL3-R15); `Module.kt`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f97d44336ce3b1437b67b2083ec01f7f3e7de6bc261111998399739097995ac6L3-R24)

### New Use Case: Mark Rule-Breaking Cells
* Added a new `MarkRuleBreakingCellsUseCase` to handle marking cells that violate game rules. This use case is integrated into the `InputNumberUseCase`. (`Module.kt`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f97d44336ce3b1437b67b2083ec01f7f3e7de6bc261111998399739097995ac6R49-R57); `InputNumberUseCase.kt`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-91e919881ffecfa5f600c53801d6a06c4a09b8c825d7258dac6a8c7a373317a0L63-R63)

These changes enhance the application's functionality by introducing a new feature for managing invalid numbers and improve the codebase's maintainability through better organization and modularity.

body: This PR adds API key authentication to `planka` using the `X-Api-Key` header. Authentication works by storing a `prefix` and hash per user. If provided the API key is checked to see if it matches the stored hash and the user is deemed authenticated. # Related Closes #945 ## Draft PR is in draft because this allows for intermediate feedback by any other contributors The frontend adds a panel to the admin actions: Which contains an overview of all current apikeys, traceable using their prefix: A menu allows for creation: Which updates the modal: allowing for cycling and deleting:

author: ksharma-xyz
body:
# Improved Android Build and Distribution Workflow

### TL;DR

Enhanced the Android build workflow with proper APK signing and improved Firebase distribution targeting.

### What changed?

- Added proper APK signing for release builds using jarsigner
- Fixed the path for release APK artifacts
- Reorganized the workflow steps for better readability
- Updated Firebase distribution to use different groups for debug vs release builds
  - Debug builds now go to "Internal" group
  - Release builds continue to go to "Friends" group
- Added a check for jarsigner availability
- Removed unnecessary directory listing steps

### How to test?

1. Trigger a debug build workflow and verify the APK is uploaded as an artifact
2. Trigger a release build workflow and verify both signed APK and AAB are uploaded as artifacts
3. Verify Firebase distribution sends debug builds to "Internal" group and release builds to "Friends" group

### Why make this change?

The previous workflow had issues with APK signing and artifact paths, causing release APKs to be unavailable or improperly signed. This change ensures that both debug and release builds are properly processed, signed, and distributed to the appropriate testing groups.

### [`v3.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/releases/tag/v3.0.0): - Upgraded Frontend, Expanded Seedfiles and much more

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/compare/v2.8.0...v3.0.0)

### 🍴🍴🍴🍴🍴🍴

#### 🚨 Breaking changes

> \[!CAUTION]
>
> ### ⚠️ Updated Admin Routes
>
> We've consolidated the admin user routes to streamline the API. The old routes under `/api/users` have been removed and replaced with new routes under `/api/admin/users`. The underlying functions are unchanged, so switching to the new routes should be seamless.
>
> - `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/admin/users`
> - `POST /api/users` → `POST /api/admin/users`
> - `GET /api/users/{item_id}` → `GET /api/admin/users/{item_id}`
> - `DELETE /api/users/{item_id}` → `DELETE /api/admin/users/{item_id}`
>
> For more info check out PR [#​5050](https://redirect.github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/issues/5050)

> \[!CAUTION]
>
> ### 🚫 Removed Backend Jinja2 Template Rendering
>
> We have removed the ability to provide and render Jinja2 templates via the backend API. This feature was never exposed in the UI and was difficult to use securely in user-facing scenarios. Users who previously relied on backend template rendering are encouraged to switch to client-side templating solutions.
>
> For more info check out PR [#​5631](https://redirect.github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/issues/5631)

#### 🎉 Highlights

##### 🆙 Frontend Upgrade to Vue 3 & Nuxt 3

We’ve successfully upgraded the Mealie frontend to Nuxt 3 and Vue 3! 🎉
This was a major overhaul that touched nearly every file in the frontend codebase. While the transition initially introduced a number of visual and functional issues, we’re confident that the vast majority have been resolved and that the new frontend is stable moving forward.
You may also notice some minor visual tweaks to make the interface more streamlined.
This upgrade significantly reduces technical debt and enables us to take advantage of the improved tooling and performance in the Nuxt 3 & Vue 3 ecosystem. We haven’t seen any remaining issues, but if you come across something that’s no longer working as it did before, we’d appreciate a heads-up!

##### 🍎 Expanded and Categorized Food Seed File

We’ve significantly increased the size of the food database — from 214 to over 2,500 foods! Additionally, all foods are now categorized, making sorted shopping lists ready to use right out of the box.
If you update your existing foods using the new seed file, please note that we do not overwrite existing entries, so some of your previously existing foods may remain uncategorized.
If you use Mealie in another language, please help us translate the new foods so everyone can enjoy the updated seed file. You can contribute translations on [Mealie’s Crowdin page](https://crowdin.com/project/mealie).
Big thanks to [@​Cameronwyatt](https://redirect.github.com/Cameronwyatt) for sticking with this through all the Crowdin limitations.

##### 🖼️ Create Recipes from Multiple Images

You can now create recipes using multiple images, making it easier to capture every step or angle of your cooking process. Along with this new feature, we’ve refreshed the visuals on the recipe creation page to provide a smoother, more intuitive experience.

##### 🔒 Option to Hide Password Login

You can now configure the frontend to hide the username and password fields on the login page by setting the environment variable `ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN` to `false`.  This streamlines the login experience for OIDC and other external auth users by removing the standard login fields.

- feat: remove unnecessary UI components if allowPasswordLogin is true [@​SurfBurger](https://redirect.github.com/SurfBurger) ([#​5484](https://redirect.github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/issues/5484))

  - Supports multi-platform builds and build caching.

- **Workflow Naming:**

- **Documentation:**

body: # Dockerize and support for local Docker deployment This PR adds Docker support to the application, preparing for containerized deployment with improved configuration management and updated tooling. This prepares for lifting into cloud services. ## Specific Changes - Added Dockerfile for containerizing the application with `uv` - For now, `bun run build` `frontend/build` and copy as-is into the container. This works because the artifact is a static site, and we don't have to have a Node/Bun runtime in the container. - Created `.dockerignore` to spare unnecessary files in the container - Added Docker startup scripts in docker/ directory for entrypoint and server initialization. Keeping this an uncomplicated Bash script for now. - Updated `justfile` for simplified task automation - Updated Python app port to 30001 to avoid colliding with macOS port 5000 which is used by [Apple AirTunes streaming](https://www.google.com/search?client=safari&rls=en&q=airtunes+5000&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8) and pre-empts `docker run --port 5000:5000` assignment ## Testing - `just build-image` then `just run` brings up the app on macOS host `localhost:5000` and it works (on my machine, need others to verify ofc) - Environment variable injection verified through groq_test.py sanity check - Frontend and backend services confirmed running on ports 30000 and 30001 respectively ### Screenshots taken from running apps inside container, accessed from Mac Host

author: orlp
body:
When using `AtomicPtr` for synchronization it's incredibly useful when you've got a couple bits you can stuff metadata in. By guaranteeing that `Thread`'s `Inner` struct is aligned to 8 bytes everyone can use the bottom 3 bits to signal other things, such as a critical section, etc.

This guarantee is thus very useful and costs us nothing.

body:
This commit adds an suggestion for an Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation.

There is a simple command line demo which uses the stdio transport protcol (there is no http transport at this point) and its usage is described in the [examples readme](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/blob/f27ace4176e2e277a6f8e4e6402c9c46711fd017/examples/mcp/README.md#whispercppexamplesmcp). The readme also contains an example of configuring Claude.ai Desktop to use this MCP server and to transcribe (please see the [Claude.ai Desktop integration section](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/blob/f27ace4176e2e277a6f8e4e6402c9c46711fd017/examples/mcp/README.md#claudeai-desktop-integration) for further details and screen shots).

The motivation for this was mainly that I wanted to learn more about MCP and trying to integrate whisper.cpp was a good way of learning. I'm not sure if this is something that we want to persue further, but I'd be happy to do so if there is interest. There are missing features of the protocol and also adding http transport (which should hopefully only be a matter of implementing a mcp::Transport for http).

----
This does not currently work on windows, and I've only tested on mac thus far.

author: hanstarj
body:
This commit adds `#[derive(Hash)]` to the `Isbn` enum.

While the underlying `Isbn10` and `Isbn13` types already derived `Hash`, the top-level `Isbn` enum did not. This prevented it from being used directly in hash-based collections like `HashMap` or `HashSet`.

This change makes the `Isbn` type more ergonomic by allowing it to be used as a key in a `HashMap`, which is a common use case.

Fixes #14

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the school activities management system, including new activity options, improved participant validation, and updates to the frontend for better participant visibility. The changes span across backend logic, frontend rendering, and styling adjustments.

### Backend Updates:
* **Added validation to prevent duplicate signups:** The `signup_for_activity` function now checks if a student is already signed up for an activity and raises an exception if so. (`src/app.py`, [src/app.pyR104-R106](diffhunk://#diff-04791d82dd15fdd480f084d7ef65a10789fa5012cb7935f76080763444d48a00R104-R106))

### New Activities:
* **Expanded activity options:** Added new activities categorized into sports, artistic, and intellectual domains, such as "Soccer Team," "Art Workshop," and "Math Olympiad," with corresponding schedules, participant limits, and initial participants. (`src/app.py`, [src/app.pyR41-R79](diffhunk://#diff-04791d82dd15fdd480f084d7ef65a10789fa5012cb7935f76080763444d48a00R41-R79))

### Frontend Enhancements:
* **Participants list rendering:** Updated the activity cards to display a list of participants or a message indicating no participants yet. This improves transparency for users viewing activity details. (`src/static/app.js`, [src/static/app.jsR23-R47](diffhunk://#diff-7146e1c8a61ac4e715182863a67d7a5a3178a73033e8344cd24f1c67787236e3R23-R47))

### Styling Improvements:
* **Styled participants section:** Added CSS rules for the participants list, including background color, borders, and typography, to ensure the section is visually distinct and user-friendly. (`src/static/styles.css`, [src/static/styles.cssR145-R173](diffhunk://#diff-090bb81494e72cfcac6b0a6065f88e9caf9d80c00b887e38f02a690dbec0f8b2R145-R173))

body:
* Allow head dims 8 and 16 in Flex backend (without compilation only)
* Minor bug fixes in Flex wrapper / backend.
* Add support for SM120, Blackwell RTX (at this time
    only [CUTLASS FNA/FMHA](https://natten.org/backends/#cutlass-fna-fmha) and
    [Flex FNA/FMHA](https://natten.org/backends/#flex-fna-fmha) backends are supported.)
* Minor bug fixes in Hopper/Blackwell FMHA.
* Removed fused additional KV from Blackwell FNA forward: no improvement in perf, complicates
    dilation, and difficult to maintain.
* **Add backward pass kernels to Hopper/Blackwell FMHA/FNA**: Both backends now support backprop,
    with the full set of features available in NATTEN. Expected performance gains compared to
    running CUTLASS (Ampere) FNA/FMHA is up to 10X (op-level). Hopper FMHA/FNA achieves more than
    50% of FAv3 backward performance, while Blackwell FMHA/FNA can in some cases even outperform
    cuDNN backward.
